title: Preparation for a simulated step
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state machine with $k>0$ work tapes over a finite alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration whose state is $q$. Suppose $a\\le c_i$ for every work-tape head position $c_i$, and every work tape is blank at coordinate $a-1$. For any natural number $n$ and integer $z$, after $k+1+(n+1)k+1$ steps from the canonical sweep configuration for $c$ with zone starting at $a$ and of size $n$, the simulator is in the right-extension phase carrying $q$ and the read table at coordinate $a+n$. Its tape has the encoded blocks with left-neighbour head flags for the zone of size $n+1$ starting at $a-1$, reversed and followed by a boundary marker on the left stack, and a boundary marker on the right stack; the input-head position and encoded output are preserved.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ has a finite state set and decidable state equality
Every work-tape head position is at least $a$
Every work tape is blank at $a-1$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a machine with $k \ge 1$ work tapes and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ in
a non-halted state $q$ such that every work-tape head of $c$ is at a coordinate at least
$a$ and every work tape of $c$ is blank at $a-1$. From the canonical between-steps
configuration for $c$ with a zone of $n$ blocks starting at $a$, running the simulator
for exactly $k + 1 + (n+1)k + 1$ transitions extends the zone by a blank block at
$a-1$, performs the forward sweep over all $n+1$ blocks — collecting the scanned symbol
of every source tape into the control and recording left-neighbour head flags in the
cells — and ends in the right-extension phase carrying $q$ and the completed read table
for coordinate $a+n$, with the read-marked encoded blocks enclosed by boundary markers
on the tape and the input head and encoded output preserved.
